name: 3D-LEX v1.0
description: In this work, we present an efficient approach for capturing sign language in 3D, introduce the 3D-LEX v1.0 dataset, and detail a method for semi-automatic annotation of phonetic properties. Our procedure integrates three motion capture techniques encompassing high-resolution 3D poses, 3D handshapes, and depth-aware facial features, and attains an average sampling rate of one sign every 10 seconds. This includes the time for presenting a sign example, performing and recording the sign, and archiving the capture. The 3D-LEX dataset includes 1,000 signs from American Sign Language and an additional 1,000 signs from the Sign Language of the Netherlands. We showcase the dataset utility by presenting a simple method for generating handshape annotations directly from 3D-LEX. We produce handshape labels for 1,000 signs from American Sign Language and evaluate the labels in a sign recognition task. reputation: A specialized sign-language dataset that is useful in sign recognition and phonetic annotation research, but not yet a broadly adopted general benchmark.
notes: Small-to-moderate scale and domain-specific; evaluation is tied to sign recognition rather than general multimodal understanding. Useful for ASL and Dutch Sign Language research.
